headline: BOTH ROUND-8 BLOCKERS ARE GENUINELY CLOSED AND EACH WAS RE-MEASURED HERE RATHER THAN READ. R8-B1: the depth bound is real and honest - over ONE 600-deep store the round-7 reader (a6b6316) completes and stands down, the round-8 reader (6cb1707) RAISES RecursionError on all four surfaces with zero stdout, and this reader completes and stands down naming incident_record_store; all four surfaces exit 0 with non-empty stdout at depths 31, 32, 33 and 600, depths 33 and 600 are BYTE-IDENTICAL on every surface over an identical root path, the predicate answers {31 True, 32 True, 33 False, 600 False}, and the frame law 5 + 2N holds EXACTLY at N = 0, 1, 2, 8, 32 with 69 at the bound. R8-B2: re-derived independently by instrumenting expect() in git worktrees at all three revisions - 3124 / 3134 / 3146, spans 22/12, 34/12 and 17/5 reproduced TO THE LABEL, the same-12 set equality TRUE, and every one of the 17 disappearances a restatement over a larger domain or a retarget carried by more teeth. The two defects this round found unprompted are real and both reproduce on the round-8 tree and are closed on this one. THE ITEM FAILS ON THE CLASS ITSELF, WHICH IS NOT CLOSED. The class R6-B1 and R8-B1 established is not `recursive reads' - it is `an exception over a recorded artifact that no handler names exits all four surfaces printing nothing', and it has TWO LIVE MEMBERS. MemoryError is named by NO handler in the pass: a SPARSE receipt file (one truncate, ZERO bytes on disk) or a sparse event stream exits all four surfaces 1 with zero stdout under a 4 GB address-space ceiling while the identical control exits 0, and naming MemoryError in the two existing handler tuples turns all four crashes into the named stand-down (measured). And .warp/metrics.py:126 reads the whole event stream inside NO try at all, so a mode-000 .warp/events.jsonl exits all four surfaces 1 with PermissionError and zero stdout - while the pass's OWN sibling reader has the named stand-down for the identical shape, and the 39-cell completeness grid misses it because it builds its model from load_events() and never runs a surface. Two prose findings besides: the manifest's bound accounting against 520badd and its 576-event committed-stream figure are both measurably wrong, with the substance behind each independently confirmed TRUE.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking - a REAL DEFECT with TWO members, and the CLASS this round's headline claims to have closed
must_fix_before_live.summary: THE DEFECT CLASS IS NOT CLOSED: TWO EXCEPTIONS OVER A RECORDED ARTIFACT STILL EXIT ALL FOUR SURFACES 1 WITH ZERO BYTES OF STDOUT, which is R6-B1's and R8-B1's exact class. (a) MEMORY ERROR IS NAMED BY NO HANDLER IN THE PASS. `MemoryError` appears ZERO times in the repository (grepped, all packs included), so it is not even a declared residual. .warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:285 names (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError) - round 9 widened that tuple for RecursionError and stopped; injecting each class through _record_shortfall shows MemoryError, TypeError, KeyError and OverflowError all ESCAPE it, and MemoryError is the one of those four a recorded artifact can actually raise. MEASURED END TO END on a relocated engine: a SPARSE receipt file in .warp/reconciliations (one `truncate`, apparent size 8 GiB, ZERO bytes on disk) exits `.warp/metrics.py`, `--json`, `.warp/dashboard.py` and `--html` EACH 1 with `MemoryError` and ZERO bytes of stdout under RLIMIT_AS 4 GiB, while the IDENTICAL control store under the IDENTICAL ceiling exits 0 on all four (text 3334, json 6198, dash 3731, html 5474 bytes); a sparse .warp/events.jsonl does the same; a sparse spec file takes the two DASHBOARD surfaces down. IDENTICAL on the round-8 tree, so this is not a round-9 regression - it is a member of the class this round says it swept from the AST. THE CEILING IS NOT ARTIFICIAL: RLIMIT_AS is what a CI container's memory limit is, and the same allocation is refused outright by this kernel with no paging for any artifact above RAM plus swap (measured: a single 200 GiB allocation returns MemoryError instantly, overcommit_memory 0). NOR IS THE SPARSE FILE NEEDED: .warp/events.jsonl is an APPEND-ONLY log the engine itself writes on every gate run, with NO rotation and NO size bound anywhere in the repository (grepped), and BOTH readers load it whole-file in ONE allocation (.warp/metrics.py:126, .warp/metrics_readers.py:151). The round's own banned-phrase register names `at any size' and `at any length' as unbounded resource domains whose SENTENCES it forbids (scripts/selftest.py:18521-18522) - and then leaves every read in the pass unbounded in size and every handler blind to the exception that domain produces. That is round 8's method lesson applied to depth only. THE HARM IS AVOIDABLE AND THE FIX FITS THE BOUNDS: adding MemoryError to the two existing handler tuples is a one-token edit on lines that already exist, so it costs NO line against metrics_read_accounting.py's 299/300 - measured on a patched copy, all four surfaces then exit 0 with non-empty stdout, renderable false, receipt_store NAMED, detail `the receipt file EXISTS and could not be read or parsed (MemoryError: ), so it authenticates nothing'. SIX sites in the pass ALREADY catch the whole Exception family for exactly this reason (the owner delegations), which is why the incident-record-store case survives and the receipt-store case does not - the asymmetry is what makes this hard to defend as deliberate. (b) .warp/metrics.py:126 `LOG.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='surrogateescape')` SITS INSIDE NO TRY AT ALL. The two handlers inside load() guard the per-line encode and the per-line json.loads only, so ANY error on the WHOLE-FILE read escapes - and every surface calls metrics.load() FIRST. MEASURED: a mode-000 .warp/events.jsonl exits all four surfaces 1 with `PermissionError` and ZERO stdout, identically at rounds 7, 8 and 9; a DIRECTORY at that path does the same with `IsADirectoryError`. (A symlink loop and a dangling symlink are fine - exists() answers False and the reader returns [].) This is R6-B1 ONE PRIMITIVE OVER: round 7 fixed the DECODE of that exact line and left the READ unguarded, and the pass's OWN sibling reader has the honest answer for the identical shape (.warp/metrics_readers.py:139-160: _present by lstat, an isfile check, read_text inside `except (OSError, ValueError)`, UNREADABLE_EVENT_STREAM named). THE SUITE CANNOT SEE IT: the 39-cell completeness grid builds its model from `R10.load_events(root)[0]` (scripts/selftest.py:15150) and never runs a CLI, so the event_stream cells prove the property over the support reader IN ISOLATION while the four surfaces on the same shape exit 1 - a property EXHIBITED over a convenient fixture rather than ENFORCED, verbatim. What the honest answer is for the LOOP reader is the owner's design call and this reviewer does not prescribe it (returning [] would be a silent zero, which is worse), but exiting 1 with nothing printed on all four surfaces is the answer two prior rounds blocked this item for.

disposition: NOT LANDED. What this round proves, and it should be said plainly because nine rounds have made it hard to see: BOTH round-8 blockers are genuinely closed, each was reproduced here on the shipped code rather than read, the depth bound is declared, honest, measured at the bound and one beyond it and at the depth that crashed, byte-identical past the bound, and sized on a frame law that is exact at every point; the label diff is now a real measurement that reproduces to the label with its set-equality claim true and all 17 disappearances checked benign; the two defects this round found without being asked are real, reproduce on the round-8 tree, and are closed here; the teeth grew correctly and the one unmutated clause is structurally unreachable, which I tested; and the per-file numstat, the module counts and the skip count are measurements now rather than inventions. Round 9 corrected its own fabrications and the new numbers are measured, with two exceptions that are R9-B2 and R9-B3. IT FAILS BECAUSE THE CLASS IS THE WRONG CLASS. The round set out to fix the defect CLASS rather than the reported instance and chose `recursive reads' as the class; the class two prior blockers actually established is `an exception over a recorded artifact that no handler names exits all four surfaces printing nothing', and that class has two live members - an artifact larger than memory, which the round's own banned-phrase list already identifies as an unbounded resource domain and then does nothing about, and a whole-file read that sits inside no try at all in the one function every surface calls first. Both are reachable, both are silent on every surface, and both have the honest answer already implemented ten lines away in the pass's own sibling reader. THE METHOD LESSON THIS ROUND ADDS: WHEN YOU DECLARE A DEFECT CLASS, DERIVE ITS BOUNDARY FROM THE HARM RATHER THAN FROM THE MECHANISM OF THE INSTANCE. R8-B1's harm was `all four surfaces print nothing where one named stand-down was honest'; its mechanism was recursion. Sweeping the mechanism found two more recursion sites and missed two non-recursion sites with the identical harm - and the sweep's own three rules (recursive library call, self-recursive call, injected callable) are visibly a mechanism taxonomy. A harm-derived rule reads instead: every handler that stands between a RECORDED ARTIFACT and a SURFACE must name every exception that artifact can produce, and every read of one must sit inside such a handler - which is checkable from the same AST the round already walks, and which fails on metrics.py:126 immediately. The second lesson is smaller: a figure read out of a file the gate mutates (.warp/events.jsonl) can never be evidence, and three rounds have now published three different values for it. THE REMAINING WORK IS ONE DESIGN DECISION (what the LOOP reader should do when the whole stream is unreadable, which is the owner's call and not the reviewer's), ONE ONE-TOKEN CODE CHANGE THAT NEEDS NO NEW LINE (MemoryError in the two handler tuples), and TWO SENTENCES.
